canonical_statement: Erdos problem 1 (erdosproblems.com/1, OPEN). The verbatim source statement: "If $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=n$ is such that the subset sums $\sum_{a\in S}a$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq A$ then\[N \gg 2^{n}.\]" In the Lean formalization (Erdos1.erdos_1) this is: there exists C > 0 (real) such that for all N : ℕ, all A : Finset ℕ with IsSumDistinctSet A N and N ≠ 0, we have C * 2 ^ A.card < N (STRICT inequality).

must_determine: an explicit constant C > 0 (necessarily C < 1/2 by the powers-of-two construction A = {1,2,4,…,2^(n−1)} with N = 2^(n−1), and C < 1 from the n = 0,1 cases with N = 1) and a proof that C·2^n < N strictly for all admissible (N, A) with N ≠ 0
the proof must eliminate the 1/√n (and any other vanishing) factor of the Erdős–Moser bound; no factor f(n) → ∞ may remain
verification that the argument handles all n uniformly, including small n and the strict inequality at the boundary
close_branch_A.statement: AFFIRMATIVE: prove the Lean statement erdos_1 verbatim — exhibit a constant C > 0 (explicit or proven to exist) such that for EVERY N ≥ 1 and EVERY A ⊆ {1,…,N} with all 2^|A| subset sums distinct, the strict inequality C·2^|A| < N holds. This is a genuine exponential lower bound with NO loss: the factor multiplying 2^n must be bounded below by a positive constant independent of n.

must_determine: an infinite family of sum-distinct sets A_i ⊆ {1,…,N_i} with |A_i| → ∞, each with a complete proof that all 2^{|A_i|} subset sums are pairwise distinct
proof that N_i / 2^{|A_i|} → 0 in the liminf sense (a rate such as C_i → 0 may accompany it but the required form is the ∀C>0 negation above, not a specific rate)
the family must satisfy A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N_i elementwise (elements ≥ 1, bounded by N_i)
close_branch_B.statement: NEGATIVE: prove the negation of the Lean statement — for every C > 0 there exist N ≥ 1 and A ⊆ {1,…,N} with all subset sums distinct such that C·2^|A| ≥ N; equivalently, along an INFINITE family of sum-distinct sets (A_i, N_i) with |A_i| → ∞ and injectivity FULLY verified for every member of the family, liminf_i N_i / 2^{|A_i|} = 0 (liminf, not lim, and not merely a sparse-subsequence artifact without the full injectivity proofs).

definitions: IsSumDistinctSet A N means A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N (every element a satisfies 1 ≤ a ≤ N; in particular 0 ∉ A and N ≥ max A when A nonempty) AND the map S ↦ ∑_{a∈S} a is injective on A.powerset (all 2^|A| subset sums, including the empty sum 0, are pairwise distinct)
n = A.card = |A|; the subset sums range over all S ⊆ A including S = ∅ (sum 0) and S = A
distinctness of subset sums is EXACT equality in ℕ/ℤ, not approximate; equivalently all 2^n subset sums are pairwise different integers

the Ω-notation N ≫ 2^n in the source statement conventionally means N ≥ c·2^n (non-strict, some absolute c > 0); the Lean formalization instead uses the STRICT form C·2^n < N. These readings differ at the boundary: a proof of the non-strict form does not literally satisfy the Lean statement, and a 'counterexample' resting on equality cases must be handled per the strict form. The close criterion is the STRICT Lean form; any non-strict proof must be upgraded or explicitly reconciled before it closes branch A
quantifier order: ∃ C > 0, ∀ N, ∀ A (uniform constant C working for every admissible pair (N, A) with N ≠ 0); N ranges over positive naturals, A over finite sets of naturals
the bound must hold for ALL n = |A| ≥ 0 (including A = ∅ and singletons, which force C < 1 since N = 1 admits A = {1} and A = ∅)
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N: every element satisfies 1 ≤ a ≤ N — no zero element, no non-positive elements, and N ≥ max A; silently allowing 0 ∈ A or elements exceeding N changes the counting range and is forbidden
EXACT pairwise distinctness of ALL 2^n subset sums (including the empty sum 0 and the full sum), as integers — no approximate or high-probability distinctness
the uniform constant C > 0 independent of n and N, with the STRICT inequality C·2^n < N per the Lean formalization
quantifier structure: ∃ C ∀ N ∀ A (with N ≠ 0); the bound must hold for every admissible pair, not almost all, not a subsequence
n = A.card is the free parameter tending over all of ℕ; no restriction on the structure of A beyond sum-distinctness and the Icc containment

A ranges over finite sets of NATURAL numbers (integrality of elements); the real-valued variant (IsSumDistinctRealSet, subset sums differing by ≥ 1) is a DIFFERENT problem and does not substitute for the integer statement
known_traps: strict-vs-nonstrict boundary: the Lean statement demands C·2^n < N strictly, while 'N ≫ 2^n' conventionally reads N ≥ c·2^n; a proof of the non-strict form, or a resolution exhibiting C ≥ 1/2 (killed by A = {1,2,4,…,2^(n−1)} with N = 2^(n−1)) or C ≥ 1 (killed by N = 1 with A = ∅ or {1}), is a failure mode
accepting a 1/poly or 1/√n (or any vanishing-factor) improvement as a close: only a constant-factor exponential bound N ≫ 2^n closes branch A; 2^n/(log n)^k, 2^n/n^ε etc. are near-misses

quantifier slip in the negative direction: the negation is ∀C>0 ∃(N,A) with C·2^|A| ≥ N, i.e. liminf N/2^n = 0 along an infinite fully-injective family; a construction with N/2^n → 0 only along a sparse subsequence, or with injectivity verified only for that subfamily, or stated as a rate C_n → 0 without establishing the ∀C negation, is not a valid close
verifying subset-sum distinctness only for small n or sampled sets and claiming it universally (sampled-to-universal)
dropping the empty subset from the distinctness check (2^n sums including 0, not 2^n − 1)
confusing the integer problem with the real variant (IsSumDistinctRealSet, gaps ≥ 1 in ℝ): bounds for one do not transfer to the other
allowing 0 ∈ A or unbounded elements in a reformulation, which changes the pigeonhole range [0, nN] underlying the trivial bound
the o(1) in the Erdős–Moser bound hides an effective threshold; treating (1/4 − o(1))·2^n/√n as a uniform-in-n bound is invalid
non_results: the trivial bound N ≫ 2^n / n (already a textbook theorem)
the Erdős–Moser bound N ≥ (1/4 − o(1))·2^n/√n and the Elkies–Gleason constant √(2/π) improvement (both already solved results)

ANY intermediate genuine improvement of the form N ≫ 2^n / f(n) with f(n) → ∞ subexponential — e.g. 2^n/(log n)^k for any fixed k, 2^n/n^ε for any ε ∈ (0,1), 2^n/exp(√(log n)), 2^n/polylog n — is a near-miss and does NOT close the problem; only a constant factor (f(n) = O(1)) closes branch A
improvements of the constant 1/4 or √(2/π) in the 2^n/√n bound
bounds valid only for restricted families of sum-distinct sets (e.g. superincreasing sequences, Conway–Guy-type constructions, geometric-progression sets)
bounds valid only along a subsequence of n, or for all sufficiently large n without covering small n (the Lean statement quantifies over all N ≠ 0 and all A)
a proof of the NON-STRICT form N ≥ c·2^n presented as matching the Lean statement verbatim without reconciling the strict inequality C·2^n < N
a proposed constant C ≥ 1/2 (refuted by A = {1,2,4,…,2^(n−1)}, N = 2^(n−1)) or C ≥ 1 (refuted by N = 1 with A = ∅ or {1})
heuristic, numerical-fit, or probabilistic-model estimates of the true growth constant
a reduction to another open problem of comparable strength (e.g. conditional on a conjecture about Sidon-set variants)
finite computations of minimal N for additional fixed n (extending A276661) without a valid finite-reduction theorem covering all n
permitted_background: the trivial counting bound 2^n ≤ nN + 1, i.e. N ≫ 2^n / n (proved in erdos_1.variants.weaker, category textbook)
the Erdős–Moser bound N ≥ (1/4 − o(1))·2^n/√n [Er56] (category research solved)
the improved constant √(2/π) via Elkies–Gleason: N ≥ (√(2/π) − o(1))·2^n/√n (category research solved)
elementary combinatorics of subset sums: pigeonhole on sums in [0, nN], injectivity of the powerset sum map
standard additive number theory techniques (Conway–Guy sequence A005318 / A276661 data on minimal N for fixed n: N(3)=4, N(5)=13, N(9)=161)
exact integer/rational arithmetic as WORLD verifier for finite checks
